activities.caption: trace the drop of blood — one full lap
activities.name: hbTraceOrder

config.prompt: A red cell makes one lap of the double circulation — put its route in order:
items: The body — then back to the right atrium
config.why: It passes through the heart TWICE per lap, and the two halves pump into separate circuits — a low-pressure lung loop and a high-pressure body loop in series.

activities.anchor: four chambers and four one-way valves
activities.caption: pair each part with its role in the beat
activities.name: hbHeartMatch

config.prompt: The self-wiring pump — pair each part with its role:

pairs.right: the self-firing spark — about every 0.8 s at rest
relays the beat after a built-in delay, so upper chambers finish emptying first

config.why: The beat runs on its own electrical system — 'lub-dub' is just the valves slamming: first the atrioventricular pair (systole), then the outlet valves.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — resting cardiac output
activities.name: hbOutputEstimate

config.prompt: Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume. At rest that is 72 beats/min × 70 mL. Roughly how many litres per minute does the heart pump?
config.why: About 5 L per minute at rest — and up to 20–30 L/min in trained athletes, most of the extra coming from a bigger stroke volume.
config.context: Exercise empties the ventricles harder and fills them deeper.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the transfusion answer
activities.name: hbGroupSpot

config.prompt: This blood answer contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Blood is a tissue: about 55% plasma and 45% cells.
Red cells are concave discs, each packing about 270 million haemoglobin molecules.
Platelets are cell fragments that trigger the clotting cascade — a fibrin plug within minutes.
Transfusing the wrong blood group is safe — the recipient's antibodies welcome the gift.
Every donated unit is typed, cross-matched and traced from vein to vein.
config.correction: The wrong blood group is lethal, not safe — the recipient's antibodies DESTROY the transfused cells.
config.why: ABO and rhesus are inherited surface-sugar variants; the antibody screen is why transfusion medicine types every unit.

activities.anchor: blood is blue inside the body
activities.caption: true or false — the colour of blood
activities.name: hbColourJudge

statements.s: Oxygen-poor blood is dark red, never blue.
statements.why: Deoxygenated blood keeps its red — darker, not a different colour.

statements.s: Veins look bluish through skin because of how light scatters in tissue and how the eye reads colour through the layers.
Blood turns red only on contact with air.
statements.why: The blue-vein diagram is a colouring convention — and no blood bank has ever drawn a blue bag.

statements.s: A red cell lives about 120 days, and the marrow replaces about 2 million per second.
statements.why: The concave discs are consumables, constantly remade.

activities.caption: the thermostat's two moves — drag from hot to cold
activities.name: hbThermoCompare

config.prompt: Thermoregulation — drag the divider across the hypothalamus's decisions:

before.label: too hot
before.text: Sweat when hot — evaporative cooling — and skin vessels flush to dump heat at the surface.

after.label: too cold
after.text: Shiver — muscle-generated heat — and skin vessels clamp, holding core temperature within about 1 °C of 37 °C.

config.why: The skin is homeostasis's largest organ — about two square metres showing the thermostat's decisions in real time, flushed, pale, sweaty or clammy.

activities.anchor: the stomach is where food is absorbed
activities.caption: route the meal — who does which job?
activities.name: hbAbsorbBranch

config.root: A meal is travelling down the nine-metre tube. Each stage of processing happens in a different organ — route it.

start.text: Which organ does acid-and-enzyme demolition and sterilisation?

choices.label: The stomach
choices.feedback: Demolition and sterilisation — its actual job.

choices.label: The small intestine
choices.feedback: That is not the demolition stage.

choices.label: The large intestine
choices.feedback: Much too late in the line.

stomach.text: Demolished. Now — where does most nutrient absorption happen?

choices.label: Along the small intestine's villi and microvilli
choices.feedback: Approaching 90% — the folded surface exists precisely to absorb.

choices.label: The stomach wall
choices.feedback: If absorption were the stomach's job, the small intestine's architecture would have no reason to exist.

si.text: Then the large intestine reclaims water and salts — the last stop before waste.

wrong1.text: The small intestine absorbs; the stomach demolishes. Route again.

wrong2.text: The large intestine reclaims water and salts only. Route again.

wrong3.text: Demolition is the stomach's job; absorption belongs to the small intestine.

config.why: Absorption is the small intestine's metres of villi and microvilli — with the large intestine reclaiming water and salts.

activities.caption: file the signs by the water loop's direction
activities.name: hbWaterBuckets

config.prompt: Osmoregulation — file each fact by which way ADH moves:

items.label: dark, scanty urine on a dehydrated day
blood too dilute after a large drink
the kidney filters about 180 L of blood daily
and reclaims about 178.5 L of it

config.why: Negative feedback like blood sugar's — needs vary with body size, climate and activity; the kidney, not a slogan, keeps the water balance.
